scheme_name: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Handloom and Other Non Farm Sector Activities
description:
The Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank scheme is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at promoting rural development through the enhancement of non-farm sector activities. 

This scheme was launched in 2006 as part of the larger strategy to empower rural communities and improve their economic conditions. 

The scheme specifically targets handloom weavers and other artisans engaged in non-farm activities. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to individuals and groups involved in handloom and other non-farm sector activities. 

The government aims to enhance the income levels of rural artisans by providing them with access to credit facilities. 

The scheme also seeks to promote self-employment opportunities among rural youth and women. 

The measurable targets include providing financial assistance to at least 10 lakh artisans by the year 2025. 

The scheme aims to increase the production capacity of handloom products by 20 percent over the next five years. 

The benefits under this scheme include loans of up to INR 1 lakh for individual artisans and INR 10 lakh for groups. 

The interest rate on loans provided under this scheme is subsidized at 7 percent per annum. 

Additionally, the government provides a credit guarantee of up to 50 percent for loans extended to artisans. 

Eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a resident of rural areas and being engaged in handloom or non-farm sector activities. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years old and should not exceed the age of 60 years. 

Income criteria stipulate that the annual income of the applicant should not exceed INR 1.5 lakh. 

Educational qualifications are not a prerequisite for eligibility under this scheme. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested applicants must approach their nearest Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank. 

They should obtain the application form from the bank or download it from the official website. 

The completed application form must be submitted along with required documents such as proof of identity, proof of residence, and income certificate. 

Additionally, applicants must provide details of their handloom or non-farm sector activities. 

Once the application is submitted, the bank will conduct a verification process. 

This process includes assessing the applicant's eligibility and the viability of the proposed activity. 

The bank will then approve the loan based on the assessment. 

Disbursement of the loan amount typically occurs within 15 days of approval. 

The frequency of loan repayment is generally set at monthly intervals. 

Repayment periods can range from 1 year to 3 years depending on the loan amount. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Cooperative Development Corporation plays a crucial role in the operational aspects of the scheme. 

Contact details for inquiries include the Ministry of Agriculture's helpline at 1800 180 1551. 

The scheme has seen a significant uptake since its launch. 

As of 2023, over 5 lakh artisans have benefited from the scheme. 

The total disbursement of loans under this scheme has exceeded INR 3,000 crores. 

The government has also introduced training programs to enhance the skills of artisans. 

These training programs are conducted in collaboration with various NGOs and cooperative societies. 

The scheme has contributed to the revival of traditional handloom practices. 

It has also aided in the preservation of cultural heritage through the promotion of handloom products. 

The government has set aside a budget of INR 500 crores for the financial year 2023-2024 specifically for this scheme. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme provides marketing support for handloom products. 

Artisans are encouraged to participate in trade fairs and exhibitions organized by the government. 

This exposure helps them reach a wider audience and increase their sales. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable practices in handloom production. 

Artisans are trained in eco-friendly techniques to ensure the sustainability of their craft. 

The government has partnered with various organizations to promote fair trade practices. 

This ensures that artisans receive a fair price for their products. 

The scheme has also been instrumental in creating awareness about the importance of handloom products. 

Efforts are underway to integrate technology into handloom production. 

This includes the use of digital platforms for marketing and selling products. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries. 

Many artisans have reported an increase in their income levels since availing of the benefits. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme through regular assessments. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme further. 

The scheme is part of the broader initiative to promote Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat. 

These initiatives aim to boost local production and reduce dependence on imports. 

The government remains committed to enhancing the livelihoods of rural artisans through this scheme. 

Overall, the Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank scheme represents a significant step towards empowering rural communities. 

It provides them with the necessary resources to thrive in the non-farm sector. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a sustainable and prosperous rural economy.
